newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares took a battering on Thursday as New Year's cheer was replaced by a festive hangover on Wall Street, dealers said.
A Tuesday night 101 point drop in New York, spurred by interest rate fears, hit global markets across Asia and Europe. South African stocks did not escape the gloom.
"The market was weak all day after Wall Street's drop," one dealer said.

The fall was accentuated by a reaction to window dressing towards the year-end as unit trusts sought to boost their books before the close of 1996. This left some shares overpriced and they took a tumble on 1997's first trading day.
The all-share index shed 40.6 points to 6,616.9 as the industrial index fell 62.1 points to 7,859.5.
Most blue-chips suffered with SAB losing 175 cents to 116.75 rand, Anglos shedding 25 cents to 257.25 rand and Iscor dropping three cents to 331 cents.
But the final scores were generally off the day's lows as industrials launched a late rally as some traders saw the market as becoming oversold.
They pointed out that underlying support looked strong for South African markets and the sector had weathered Thursday's storm better than most European bourses.
"It's not been too bad at all really. We have lost less than most other markets," one dealer said.

Volumes were modest at around the 200 million rand worth of shares changing hands. Dealers were split on prospects for Friday with some saying the market could bounce and others saying any recovery would wait until the middle of the month.
The gold index had a rough day as bullion prices started to slip. London gold was fixed at its lowest level since December 3, 1996, after a late sell-off in new York on Tuesday.
The golds index lost 1.2 percent, or 18.1 points, to end at 1,488.1.
South African early futures also took a knock from Wall Street's drop, but hit support by noon and launched a late recovery -- though they did not regain all their losses.
The all-share March contract dipped to 6,090/115 from 6,160 as the industrials contract fell to 7,615/630 from 7,698. The gold contract was becalmed at 1,040/50 from 1,060.
